title: Cross-tenant trace corruption detection and hotpath latency/error dashboard
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: In Dedicated and Private deployments we occasionally see traces that appear to be 'corrupted' across tenant boundaries (mismatched trace IDs, truncated spans, or duplicated root spans) which cause root-cause analysis to be misleading in customer dashboards and occasionally surface as incorrect latency attribution. This ticket implements a cross-tenant trace corruption detector + a hotpath latency/error dashboard for Dedicated/VPC/on-prem collectors to: (1) detect and surface corrupted traces early; (2) show tenant-scoped hotpaths contributing to tail latency/errors; (3) protect multi-tenant isolation guarantees by flagging collector misrouting or envelope mangling. The detector is implemented as a lightweight validation pass in the on-prem/VPC collector binary and as a runtime hook in the serving runtime to attach verification metadata (signed trace_digest headers). The dashboard aggregates corruption-rate, percentiles for hot spans, error counts by model/route, and shows correlated log snippets and KV-cache miss spikes for fast triage.
acceptance_criteria: Collector validation pass rejects or marks traces with corrupted/invalid trace IDs and emits a corruption metric with tenant and node tags
Serving runtime adds optional signed-trace-digest header and a verification flag in telemetry; backwards compatible when disabled

Console dashboard has a dedicated view for Dedicated / Private pools showing corruption rate, top 10 hotpaths (span name + route), 95/99 latency and error trends, and hyperlinks to trace links and log snippets
End-to-end test exists that simulates envelope mangling and verifies detection, metric emission, and dashboard visibility
Feature can be toggled per-customer via console toggle and rolled out to a single Dedicated pool for canary
notes: Design tradeoffs: strong verification (signing) reduces false positives but adds ~0.5-1ms per request in worst-case for signing checks; we default to opt-in for Private and enable for Dedicated by policy

We considered full OTEL schema validation in the collector but rejected it because of collector CPU overhead on high-throughput tenants; instead we do focused checks (trace_id entropy, span parent-child consistency, timestamp monotonicity) and a compact digest signature for critical paths
Privacy: any trace-digest or signed header must not contain PII; we will use a deterministic hash over non-PII span identifiers plus a rotating node key stored via KMS for Private installs

Rollout plan: (1) internal canary on staging dedicated pool; (2) invite-list for beta customers with traffic mirror; (3) opt-in for Private customers with consul/helm flag; (4) force-enable only for customers under investigation with signed approval
Open questions: key rotation cadence for on-prem KMS stores, how aggressively to sample traces used for signature verification, and retention policy for corrupted-trace artifacts
